## What We Did

Learned about spatial joins in R using the sf library. We also explored a significant side tangent on the topic of projections, and how to use them to make maps more accurate.

## Key Concepts

CRS: Coordinate Reference System, a way to describe how the two-dimensional, projected map in your GIS relates to real places on the earth.
two types of crs:
- Geographic: exists on an approximate sphere measured in degrees of latitude and longitude. Not good for measuring distances or areas.
- Projected: exists on a flat surface measured in meters or feet. Good for measuring distances

Common coordinate systems:
- EPSG 2272: Pennsylvania South (ftUS)
- UTM: Universal Transverse Mercator, a system of 60 zones that each have their own projection
- EPSG 5070: NAD83 / Conus Albers, a projection that is good for the contiguous United States
- EPSG 4326: WGS 84, a geographic coordinate system that is used by GPS

st_set_crs() - set the crs of a spatial object (no numbers changed)
st_transform() - transform the crs of a spatial object (numbers changed)
st_crs(): returns the crs of a spatial object

st_buffer() - creates a buffer around a spatial object
st_intersection() - returns the intersection of two spatial objects
st_distance() - returns a matrix of distances between 2 spatial objects
